insights.headline: Banks push back on RBI's FX curbs as MCX gold trails global gains ahead of Dhanteras
insights.summary: Banks have asked the RBI to soften its weekend rupee-defence package — a 20% cash-deposit rule on FX derivatives and a $2 million threshold — even as the rupee opened 1% stronger at 95.76 per dollar. Global gold held near $4,200 on easing inflation fears while MCX December gold slipped to about Rs 1,50,845 per 10 grams; spot gold sits roughly 23% below its record high ahead of Dhanteras on November 6. Record September inflows into Indian gold and silver ETFs and China's 23-tonne September purchase showed investors and central banks buying the dip, with Wednesday's US CPI the week's key event.
points: Banks seek relief from RBI's 20% FX-derivative deposit rule; rupee opened 1% higher at 95.76/$.
Global gold near $4,200–4,230 on easing inflation fears; MCX Dec gold ~Rs 1,50,845/10g.
Spot gold ~23% below its record high of $5,417; MCX futures 16% off peak with Dhanteras on Nov 6.
India gold ETF inflows hit a record Rs 8,363 cr in Sept; silver ETFs drew Rs 5,341 cr as equities lagged.
China bought 23t of gold in Sept, its biggest monthly haul in ~3 years; reserves hit a record 2,410t.

trending.title: The rupee fights back — and banks push back
trending.summary: RBI's weekend FX package pulled USD/INR 1% stronger to 95.76, cutting bullion import costs — but banks want the 20% cash-deposit rule on FX derivatives softened or replaced with a flat charge.

trending.title: MCX trails the world
trending.summary: Comex gold rose toward $4,229 as inflation fears eased while MCX gold slipped intraday — the rupee's jump is doing part of the divergence work, and Kedia Advisory flags Rs 1,50,870 as key support.

trending.title: Buying the dip before Dhanteras
trending.summary: Gold sits about 23% below its record high with Dhanteras on November 6; Mirae Asset's new report says surging US yields explain the correction without breaking gold's longer-term case.

trending.title: Paper gold goes mainstream in India
trending.summary: Record September ETF inflows — Rs 8,363 cr into gold, Rs 5,341 cr into silver — show Indian investors rotating out of weak equities; WGC data shows Indian gold ETF holdings up 31% since December.

trending.title: Central banks keep buying the dip
trending.summary: China's 23-tonne September purchase — its biggest in about three years and its 23rd straight month of buying — took reserves to a record 2,410t, closing in on France and Italy for the top three.

items.title: Banks seek RBI relief, clarity on India's latest rupee-defence measures, sources say
items.summary: Banks have asked the RBI to ease the 20% cash-deposit rule on FX derivatives used to hedge current-account exposures and scrap the $2 million threshold, proposing a flat charge instead, sources told Reuters. Lenders say the deposit would tie up rupee liquidity — Citi estimates ₹60,000–70,000 crore could be absorbed. The rupee still jumped 1% to 95.76 on Monday; the RBI did not comment.

items.title: Gold, silver gain globally on easing inflation fears, trade lower on MCX
items.summary: Comex gold futures traded near $4,229 an ounce and silver near $61.28 as expectations that Russia would supply diesel eased inflation concerns, while on MCX the December gold contract slipped to about Rs 1,50,845 per 10 grams and silver to Rs 2,25,304 per kg. Kedia Advisory's Ajay Kedia pointed to short covering on MCX, putting gold support at Rs 1,50,870 and resistance at Rs 1,51,915.

items.title: Gold Prices Fall Ahead of Dhanteras: Why It Remains a Smart Long-Term Investment
items.summary: With Dhanteras on November 6, spot gold trades near $4,185 an ounce — about 23% below this year's record high of $5,417 — while MCX December futures sit near Rs 1,50,001 per 10 grams, 16% off their peak. Mirae Asset's 'Why Gold ETF Now?' report says rising US 10-year yields (5.27%) explain the correction without undoing gold's longer-term case, citing central-bank buying and festive demand.

items.title: Gold prices fall Rs 1,450/10g; silver down Rs 1,400/kg despite a soft dollar ahead of US economic data. Time to sell?
items.summary: MCX December gold futures fell ₹1,450 to ₹1,51,499/10g and silver dropped ₹1,400 to ₹2,24,326 per kg on Monday as investors awaited US inflation data. Spot gold rose 0.3% to $4,206.01 and silver added 0.5% to $61.12. Prithvi Finmart's Manoj Kumar Jain put MCX gold support at ₹1,50,500–1,49,800 and resistance at ₹1,52,000–1,52,850; traders see 17% odds of an October Fed hike, 86% by December.

items.title: What investors should do as inflows into gold, silver ETFs scale record highs
items.summary: Net inflows into Indian gold ETFs hit a record ₹8,363 crore in September (from ₹2,189 crore in August) while silver ETFs drew ₹5,341 crore, AMFI data showed, as investors rotated out of volatile equities. Silver ETFs opened Thursday at a 10–12% premium to spot on industrial demand; Kotak suspended lumpsum investments into its Silver ETF Fund of Fund on October 9 amid a domestic supply shortage.

items.title: China now fifth largest gold holder, could beat France and Italy to enter top 3 spot this year, finds data — All we know
items.summary: China's central bank bought 23 tonnes of gold in September — its biggest monthly purchase in about three years and its 23rd straight month of buying — lifting reserves to a record 2,410 tonnes, per Kobeissi Letter data cited by Mint. China is now the fifth-largest official holder; with France at 2,437t and Italy at 2,452t, it could claim No. 3 this year at ~20t a month.

items.title: Gold gains on weaker oil, dollar; US inflation data in focus
items.summary: Gold rose 0.3% to $4,206.01 on Monday as falling oil and a softer dollar lifted bullion into the week's US inflation data. Oil slid after Trump's announced Russia-Ukraine energy ceasefire; silver added 0.5% to $61.12. Traders await Wednesday's CPI and Thursday's PPI and retail sales, pricing a 17% Fed-hike chance in October and 86% by December.

items.title: Gold Prices Down 4%, Fuels Selective Buying
items.summary: Gold is down nearly 4% in a month to about ₹1.47 lakh per 10 grams from ₹1.53 lakh, spurring selective buying ahead of the peak festive and wedding season, the Economic Times reports. Buyers favour lightweight, lower-carat and studded designs plus old-gold exchanges; CaratLane's Saumen Bhaumik said demand is deliberate but resilient across segments.

items.title: Gold and silver price forecast: key breakout levels to watch before September CPI
items.summary: Gold held near $4,210 and silver near $61 on Monday as markets counted down to Wednesday's September CPI. In FXEmpire's technical view, gold needs a confirmed break above $4,250 to target $4,330 (support $4,100); silver must clear $62.60 before testing $64-65. With ~85% odds of a December Fed hike priced in, a hot CPI could lift the dollar and yields; a soft one gives both metals room to recover.

items.title: Silver Price Forecast, Prediction: $70 December Target Faces Demand Test
items.summary: Spot silver closed around $60.83, up about 2.2% on the day, as the market tests whether the rebound can reach $70 by December. UBS holds forecasts of $70/oz for December 2026 and $80 for September 2027; Goldman Sachs estimated roughly $1.6bn of speculative silver selling during September 22-29, framing the December target as a test of real demand.

items.title: Gold jewellers brace for Q3 after growth cools in Q2
items.summary: Mint reports gold retailers posted strong but slower Q2 growth — Titan's jewellery revenue rose 25%, Kalyan Jewellers over 26%, Senco 29% at retail — as the festive season slipped into the December quarter. Jewellers bet on Dhanteras, Diwali and about 13.5 million weddings in 2026, though Crisil says value growth still outpaces volume with 24k gold above ₹1,50,000 per 10g.
